statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Let P_0 be the length-m sequence [1,2,...,m], so P_0[j] = j+1 for 0 <= j < m. For each i with 0 <= i < n, let p_i be the unique index with 0 <= p_i < m and P_i[p_i] = queries[i], and let P_{i+1} be the length-m sequence obtained by moving the element at index p_i of P_i to the front: P_{i+1}[0] = queries[i], P_{i+1}[j] = P_i[j-1] for 1 <= j <= p_i, and P_{i+1}[j] = P_i[j] for p_i < j < m. Then len(r) = n and for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = p_i.
preconditions: m is an integer with 1 <= m <= 1000; n = len(queries) satisfies 1 <= n <= m; and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= queries[i] <= m.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries) such that q = queries[i] occurs earlier in queries, let j be the largest index with 0 <= j < i and queries[j] = q. Then r[i] equals the number of distinct values that occur among queries[j+1],...,queries[i-1]; this number is 0 when j+1 > i-1.

statement: Let n = len(queries) and define P_0,...,P_n by the move-to-front rule starting from P_0 = [1,2,...,m]. Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] is a valid index into P_i and P_i[r[i]] = queries[i].
